for: A slide of its own in the presentation (edition 08 has it as slide 9).
shows: One corner of the room growing, from the timber standing bare through each summer to the last, three times over: three grown runs of the same planting on the same building with the same care, differing only in the simulator's chance. Then the three last summers in turn. The timber is the same every time and the plants are not. On paper the same band of each last summer stands one above another.
statement: A growth scenario on stated assumptions, not a forecast. Concept geometry; trial planting.

words.title: Grown three times
now: The timber goes up. The plants go in and grow.
The same room again. Nothing is changed.
The same timber every time. Never the same plants.
card: One room is grown three times on a computer, with nothing changed between them.
Timber designed for plants we cannot control.
How much real plants vary. The simulator's plant numbers are assumptions.
words.alt: One corner of a timber room. Climbing plants grow over it from bare timber to full summer, three times. The timber is the same each time; the plants end up different each time.
